framing.statement: Section 12.10 defines device-originated segment 111 in data section 3: required Segment Type 111 and three-character Segment Length precede repeated required three-character Elements 111 and 112 and variable Element 113. Segment Length includes Segment Type and separators. Segment maximum is 999; repeated information section maximum is 991 bytes including the final separator. Separators follow Segment Type and Segment Length and the final information section, but not the elements within or the repetitions of that section. Local examples containing plus signs between table ID, length and payload must not silently override this explicit framing definition.

testDesign.positive: One segment with two contiguous table records 050004ABCD051004WXYZ and one final separator; count complete segment bytes including its header separators.
testDesign.negative: Insert a separator between 050 and its length only; observe a framing discrepancy against 12.10, without inventing a host response code.
testDesign.boundary: Compare information-section lengths 991 and 992, and complete segment lengths 999 and 1000.
testDesign.notes: Length counts are wire bytes, not the count of rendered placeholder characters. Local attribute and example conflicts remain review-only.

references.statement: Common Element 111/112/113 ordering and repeated-record framing.

Special Payments Indicator has R for recurring and I for installment. R applies only to credit card type 020 with a Visa, MasterCard, Discover or Amex BIN. The local Table Length attribute a1 is not silently substituted for the common three-character Element 112.

Ten-character POS Condition Code is required for EMV, internet/mobile/ecommerce/in-app and Credential-on-File transactions, optional otherwise. Source positions are terminal class 1-2, presentation 4-7, security 8 and terminal type 9-10; the local list omits position 3. Visa terminal types 25 or 26 require CAVV. Appendix Q supplies terminal codes.

Appendix Q describes terminal type 25 as secure Internet using Verified by Visa or 3DES and labels it nonrecurring. Table 056 explicitly uses 25 for authenticated India recurring events; retain both descriptions, not an invented exclusion.

Verified by Visa payload is raw binary: XID 20 bytes then CAVV 20 bytes, maximum 40. Raw bytes are not substituted with hexadecimal or base64 text. Appendix Y describes cryptogram choice; the revised CAVV in segment 123 is a separate representation.

Section 12.19 requires segment 123 for initial and recurring tokenized transactions and MasterCard Token/DSRP or Visa TAVV data. Element 237 carries request-only TAVV in 28-byte base64 format with alphabet a-z, A-Z, 0-9, +, =, /. Element 195 is a separate 20-byte revised CAVV representation. Segment fields have separators even when unpopulated.

MasterCard token/DSRP cryptograms belong in segment 123 Element 237; AAV belongs in segment 111 Table 036. When both DSRP and AAV are sent, UCAF security-level positions 1-2 are 21. Visa support for separate token TAVV and 3DS CAVV is described as effective October 2018, subject to First Data availability; usage grid is explicitly nonexhaustive. Verified-by-Visa-only uses Table 035; wallet scenarios use revised CAVV 195, with TAVV 237 for the combined scenario.

Use Appendix D's alphabetical state codes for a space-padded subdivision, not its numeric ANSI terminal identifiers. Defined alphabetical codes are preserved below. The outside-US/Canada NA entry and ISO3166-2 discussion are context-specific; they do not establish a worldwide service-location code list.

Appendix AC is the referenced numeric country-code authority for Tables 059 and 064/03, but its heading describes the acquiring institution's country. Preserve that contextual mismatch with retailer/service location. Examples: Canada 124, India 356, US 840, Puerto Rico 630. N/A and the unnumbered Antarctica entry do not constitute n3 wire values. Source entries such as American Samoa 840, Mauritania 929 and Sao Tome and Principe 930 must not be repaired from an external standard.

Actual Enabler Verification Value layout is Table 071 with fixed length 005 and five alphanumeric bytes for Visa/Interlink. Table 065's note instead calls it Sub Table 64. Do not relabel Table 064 or populate EVV in 065.

Element111 is AN, fixed3, identifying the variable-information type; its code list defines050-060 and062-067, not061. Element112 is N,fixed3, valid001-999, and counts Element113. Element113 is AN,max982 and points to12.10 for length conditions; selector determines payload meaning. Specific appendix declarations, including binary035 and space exceptions, are preserved rather than filtered by generic AN.

Financial requests have section1 Version Identifier55/Number of Segments63, section2 Standard Message Data Segment100 and section3 none,one or more chapter12 segments, including111. Table presence does not imply segment111 must occur in every financial transaction.

Account updater participation requires a participating acquirer,CNP credential-on-file/installment/recurring context, and merchant registration/certification with First Data. Participating merchants should send060/01 as trigger for all these contexts; First Data determines qualification before requesting association updates. AD refers to Elements2 and12 for credential/expiration-date handling and to Account Representative for details.

Following a segment155 account update, a follow-on may use original or new PAN,or original/new TransArmor token as TAP. Element12's expiration date should correspond to the selected PAN/token in Element2; either original/new expiry is permitted in follow-on context. Retry of follow-on reversal,completion,cancellation,Void of Merchandise Return or timeout reversal must preserve initial-attempt credentials. For either TransArmor method,expiry belongs in Element12 and is stored for token-associated follow-ons.

Section12.39 response segment155 is permitted only when Auth Optimizer qualifies and is used; absent fields are omitted without separators. Defined response records are001 updated PAN(an19,max19,Y only,not token-based),002 updated TransArmor token(an19,max19,Y only,not PAN-based),003 expiry(an4,fixed004,YYMM,Y only),004 status(An1,fixed001,Y/I;A new account+expiry,E new expiry,Q contact cardholder,C closed,U unknown),005 original association decline(an4,max4 but length line says variable3,Y/I only following decline and optimizer-directed reattempt),006 result(an6,fixed006,Y/I,Visa only). First five records are Visa/MasterCard. Results are VAU001 token,002 non-Visa PAN,003 unsupported network,004 nonqualifying original transaction category,005 CVV2 present,006 nonqualifying type,007 MCC unsupported,008 acquirer/processor inactive,009 issuer unsupported,010 issuer/Visa merchant block,011 PPCS stop order,012 credentials already latest,013 request expiry later than VAU,014 PAN opt-out,016 PAN stop advice. VAU015 is not defined.

Estimated/incremental authorization for MCC4121 and5411 is CNP-only; MCC5552 identifies EV. For permitted merchants when final amount is unknown,initial/estimated request includes estimated indicator. Increment follows initial/estimated authorization and uses its approval code for host incremental identification,and matching Sequence Number,Transaction Identifier and Table063 Terminal Transaction Number. Example initial Acquirer Trace09 indicator1 is not carried on subsequent increments; final amount is sent in completion. Cruise,lodging,car/vehicle rental approvals expire14 days after initial estimated auth; other rental such as campgrounds/trailer parks expire7 days after initial. For longer stays complete first transaction and start second on/before applicable day14/day7 to avoid the described no-authorization chargeback exposure.

limitations: Independent source-derived draft, not approval, certification, executable coverage or reviewed TS/TC/TD.
No AI artifacts or overview oracle were read. The appendix inventory is navigation-only and is used solely for identity validation.
No Table 061 or allocated-but-undefined nested IDs are invented. Table 063 has positional fields, not defined sub-table selectors.

Table060's local definition describes updates only if available. Referenced section12.39 defines returned YYMM expiry and Elements2/12 define follow-on/retry credential matching; Appendix AE adds category-specific7/14-day approval expiry for Table063 context. These are not a universal card-expiration validator. The referenced Visa dual-cryptogram functionality date is October2018; no additional effective date is invented.

External RBI revisions, Global BIN File, UCOM assignments, network-assigned gateway IDs, USPS/country postal standards and cryptographic standards are unavailable here; dependent cases require review.
Negative cases describe review discrepancies or missing expected effects, not invented response codes. Synthetic raw cryptograms are layout examples only and do not establish cryptographic validity.

fields.requiredness: Presence is not mandated here; data required if table sent

rules.statement: When the terminal supplies an additional security code, Table 050 has a three-digit selector and three-digit payload-length field; its alphanumeric payload is 1-16 bytes, and SVS requires exactly four.

testDesign.positive: SVS fixture uses 050004A7B9; non-SVS uses 050001A.
testDesign.negative: Change only SVS payload and its declared count to five alphanumeric bytes; observe an SVS-length discrepancy.
testDesign.boundary: Non-SVS lengths 1 and 16 versus 0 and 17; SVS 3/4/5. Independently mutate Element 112 from 004 to 003 for four bytes.
testDesign.notes: No rule here makes Table 050 universally mandatory; common framing is ATL105-12.10.

fields.requiredness: Not universally required; merchant-provided when present

rules.statement: A merchant-provided additional card ID uses Table 051, a three-digit payload length and 1-16 alphanumeric bytes; SVS card transactions instead require exactly four payload bytes.

testDesign.positive: SVS uses 051004ID07; non-SVS uses 051016ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOP.
testDesign.negative: Replace only SVS four-byte ID with three bytes and update its count; observe SVS-length discrepancy.
testDesign.boundary: Non-SVS 1/16 valid versus 0/17; SVS 3/4/5; declared 003 with four bytes is a separate length defect.
testDesign.notes: Not the same field as Table 050; do not transfer additional-security semantics.

rules.statement: Table 052 carries at most 100 units described as digits in an an100 TLV payload. Each defined nested record has its two-character ID, three-digit length and alphanumeric data, with limits 40 for KSN and 8 for Device Type. The sentence saying the first three digits are length is retained as a framing ambiguity, not used to reverse the displayed nested field order.

testDesign.positive: Logical payload 01004ABCD02003NCR is 17 bytes and follows the displayed ID-length-data order.
testDesign.negative: Keep data fixed and change KSN nested count 004 to 005; observe nested framing mismatch.
testDesign.boundary: KSN 40/41 and Device Type 8/9; aggregate 100/101 only if additional records are independently authorized.
testDesign.notes: Do not invent additional sub-tables to reach the aggregate limit. Resolve the first-three-digits wording before wire execution.

rules.statement: AES DUKPT, TDES and Ingenico OnGuard each require KSN sub-table 01; Device Type 02 is additionally required for AES DUKPT but optional for TDES and OnGuard.

testDesign.positive: AES DUKPT request contains 01 KSN and 02 device; TDES and OnGuard fixtures each contain KSN with Device Type omitted.
testDesign.negative: Remove only Device Type from the AES fixture; observe missing required encryption metadata.
testDesign.boundary: Remove KSN separately from each of the three types; optional-device omission in TDES must not fail the AES-only condition.
testDesign.notes: Synthetic KSN exercises presence and length, not key derivation or cryptographic correctness.

notes.statement: The Appendix I-54 example shows ID-length-data concatenation and a 037-byte Table 052 payload; plus delimiters around this example do not override section 12.10.

fields.requiredness: Applicable only to MasterCard when DSRP or TAVV is also sent in segment 123; no universal must-send stated

rules.statement: The remote commerce acceptor identifier is the consumer-visible merchant checkout identifier, such as URL or reverse domain, base64 encoded with a maximum of 28 characters.

testDesign.positive: MasterCard qualifying fixture shows merchant identifier shop.test during checkout and transmits c2hvcC50ZXN0 (12 encoded characters).
testDesign.negative: Change only wire representation to unencoded shop.test; observe encoded-representation discrepancy.
testDesign.boundary: 28 versus 29 encoded characters, not decoded URL length; empty-value permissibility is unspecified.
testDesign.notes: Whether 028 measures encoded or decoded size needs review; enforce no repaired interpretation automatically.

rules.statement: Table 053 applies only to MasterCard requests also sending DSRP or TAVV data in segment 123. MasterCard token/DSRP belongs in Element 237, not UCAF Table 036; simultaneous AAV and DSRP uses UCAF security-level 21.

testDesign.positive: MasterCard ecommerce request contains 053 and segment 123/237 with a 28-byte base64 token cryptogram; a separate AAV, if present, uses Table 036 and level 21.
testDesign.negative: Remove only segment 123 cryptogram from the qualifying Table 053 request; observe missing applicability companion.
testDesign.boundary: Visa with the same TAVV companion is outside Table 053 scope; DSRP-only and TAVV-only companions each qualify.
testDesign.notes: No requirement to send 053 in every MasterCard transaction is inferred; cryptogram validity requires authorized external fixtures.

rules.statement: For a qualifying Table 053 request, the segment 123 Element 237 token/DSRP companion is request-only, fixed 28 bytes in base64 form. It is distinct from the base64 merchant identifier in Table 053 and from binary XID/CAVV in Table 035. Appendix Y routes MasterCard AAV to UCAF and token/DSRP to Element 237.

testDesign.positive: Structural MasterCard request has Table 053 checkout identifier c2hvcC50ZXN0 and a separate 28-character base64 Element 237 consisting of 27 A characters followed by =; the cryptogram is synthetic, not issuer-valid.
testDesign.negative: Change only the last Element 237 character from = to ?, retaining length 28; observe character outside its listed base64 alphabet.
testDesign.boundary: Element 237 width 28 versus 27/29; its 28-byte ceiling is independent of the merchant identifier's 28-character ceiling.
testDesign.notes: Network cryptogram generation and authentication need external authorized fixtures; a structurally valid base64 string is not proof of cryptographic validity. Payload + characters are data within counted fields, not a reason to split raw field content.

fields.length: variable up to 95 bytes; Moneris maximum 15
fields.requiredness: Mandatory for Moneris; otherwise merchant assigned if present

rules.statement: Table 054 carries the merchant-assigned transaction identifier, up to 95 ans bytes. For Moneris it is mandatory, limited to 15 and mapped to Client Request ID 7b.

testDesign.positive: Moneris uses merchant ID M00000000000001 (15 bytes) and observes identical Client Request ID 7b downstream.
testDesign.negative: Remove only Table 054 from Moneris request; observe missing required Client Request ID input.
testDesign.boundary: Moneris 15/16 and non-Moneris 95/96; absent non-Moneris is not rejected by this source alone.
testDesign.notes: Downstream mapping requires an observable Moneris test environment; no truncation behavior is specified.

fields.length: variable up to 4 bytes; all listed values have 4

rules.statement: Table 055 conveys the UCOM-provided Experience Provider value, up to four alphanumeric bytes. Defined codes are WMPY (Walmart+), AAPY (Amazon Pay), GSPY (Google Pay) and WXPY (Wex Pay).

testDesign.positive: UCOM fixture assigns GSPY and Table 055 transmits 004GSPY; separately exercise each of the other three listed codes.
testDesign.negative: Change only code to four-byte ZZZZ; observe an unlisted provider value.
testDesign.boundary: Listed four-byte code versus truncated three-byte GSP and five-byte GSPYX.
testDesign.notes: No new UCOM codes or mandatory presence are inferred.

rules.statement: Table 056 has maximum 200 bytes of stored-credential MIT/CIT data. Nested format is n2 ID, n2 length in 01-35, and up to 35 an bytes; individual layouts refine types and lengths. The allocated ID range 01-24 is not a list of defined layouts: only 01-09,12,13 are defined here. Populate only transaction-applicable records.

testDesign.positive: Logical Discover first-payment count record is 010202, with outer 056006 for its six-byte payload.
testDesign.negative: Change only nested length from 02 to 03 while retaining two count bytes; observe nested framing mismatch.
testDesign.boundary: Nested allocation 01/35 versus 00/36; do not treat undefined selector 10 as a defined business layout. Aggregate maximum 200/201 without fabricating extra records.
testDesign.notes: The generic an description does not erase the ans20 Validation Reference declaration.

rules.statement: Discover total payment count 01 is two bytes: 02-99, UD for undefined, or UC for until canceled. It applies only to the first recurring/installment payment.

testDesign.positive: Discover first installment sends 01 length 02 data 02; separately exercise 99, UD and UC.
testDesign.negative: Change only count 02 to 01; observe value outside Discover count domain.
testDesign.boundary: 02/99 inclusive; 01/00 outside. Sending the same count on a subsequent payment is a distinct phase discrepancy.
testDesign.notes: Do not interpret 99 as Discover undefined; UD and UC have that meaning.

rules.statement: Visa total payment count 01 uses two digits 01-98, or 99 for undefined/until canceled. This field is required and should be sent only for recurring payments on India-issued Visa cards.

testDesign.positive: India-issued Visa recurring registration includes 01 with count 01 or sentinel 99.
testDesign.negative: Change only count to UD; observe Visa-domain discrepancy.
testDesign.boundary: 01/98/99 versus 00; omission and non-India inclusion are separate requiredness/scope mutations.
testDesign.notes: MasterCard does not inherit count rules.

rules.statement: Payment Type 02 is one byte F for fixed amount or V for variable amount, and applies only to Discover and Visa. Discover uses it only on the first recurring/installment payment; Visa requires it only for India-issued recurring payments.

testDesign.positive: Discover first recurring payment sends F; India-issued Visa recurring registration sends V.
testDesign.negative: Change only V to X; observe unlisted payment-type value.
testDesign.boundary: One byte versus two; Discover subsequent payment with 02 is outside its first-only scope.
testDesign.notes: Visa requiredness does not apply to Visa non-India/nonrecurring requests.

rules.statement: MIT Amount 03 is twelve numeric characters, leading-zero padded with two decimal places, in the transaction amount's currency. It may differ from the transaction amount. It is Discover/Visa only and required only for India-issued Visa recurring payments.

testDesign.positive: Recurring amount USD 50.00 uses 000000005000 even if this transaction's USD charge is 1.00.
testDesign.negative: Change only one amount character to a decimal point; observe nonnumeric amount representation.
testDesign.boundary: Twelve digits versus 11/13; zero and all-nine wire values test width only, not authorized financial limits.
testDesign.notes: No general Discover first-only condition is stated for this amount; unlike Table 067 the text explicitly says two decimals.

rules.statement: Discover-only Unique ID 04 is a fourteen-byte alphanumeric merchant identifier for each recurring/installment payment, used to reference authorizations and advice messages.

testDesign.positive: Discover installment uses ID ABCDEFGHIJKLMN and its advice references that same merchant payment identifier.
testDesign.negative: Change only brand to Visa while retaining 04; observe Discover-only applicability discrepancy.
testDesign.boundary: 14 versus 13/15 bytes; no lifetime uniqueness algorithm is specified.
testDesign.notes: Do not confuse this merchant ID with UUID or Visa Registration Reference Number.

rules.statement: Frequency 05 is two digits. Discover codes 01-08 mean daily, weekly, biweekly, monthly, quarterly, half-yearly, annually and unscheduled, respectively, and are first-payment only. Visa additionally allows 09 ten days, 10 twice weekly, 11 every two months and 12 trimester; Visa requires this field only for India-issued recurring payments.

testDesign.positive: Discover first payment uses 08 for unscheduled; Visa India recurring uses 09 for ten days.
testDesign.negative: Change only Discover frequency from 08 to 09; observe brand-specific domain violation.
testDesign.boundary: Discover 01/08 and Visa 01/12; 00/13 are unlisted. Test all twelve source meanings independently.
testDesign.notes: First-only Discover scope does not transfer to Visa subsequent payments.

rules.statement: Validation Flag 06 has one digit: 1 validated or 0 not validated, Discover/Visa only. Discover describes checking against a validation source; Visa describes offline validation during registration and requires the field only for India-issued recurring payments.

testDesign.positive: Visa India registration validated offline sends 1; an unvalidated registration sends 0 without implying authentication succeeded.
testDesign.negative: Change only flag to 2; observe unlisted validation flag.
testDesign.boundary: One numeric digit; 0 and 1 have different validation-source preconditions.
testDesign.notes: This flag is not proof of successful issuer authentication or authorization.

rules.statement: For Visa India recurring, fields 01,02,03,05 and 06 supplied initially must also appear on every subsequent transaction, using their original value or the value from the last Modification transaction. Registration Reference Number 13 instead retains the initial value even after modification.

testDesign.positive: Initial agreement frequency 04 changes to 02 in a successful Modification fixture; next payment uses 02 and retains its initial 35-byte registration reference. Repeat history case independently for count, payment type, amount and flag.
testDesign.negative: Change only subsequent frequency to 01, which matches neither initial nor last modification; observe history mismatch.
testDesign.boundary: No modification means initial values; multiple modifications use latest. Omit one initially supplied field at a time.
testDesign.notes: The text says original OR last-modification value; do not silently strengthen it to latest-only. Modification success semantics are not defined here.

rules.statement: Validation Reference 07 is a twenty-byte ans cryptogram generated by the validation source for each cardholder account to let the issuer validate the transaction; it applies only to Discover.

testDesign.positive: Discover structural fixture sends 20-byte synthetic reference ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRST from its stub validation source.
testDesign.negative: Change only brand to Visa retaining 07; observe out-of-brand reference.
testDesign.boundary: 20 versus 19/21 bytes; an ans byte must not be rejected solely because the general nested-format note says an.
testDesign.notes: Synthetic text does not establish a genuine cryptogram; external validation-source requirements remain review-only.

rules.statement: Discover Sequence Indicator 08 is two numeric digits, identifying multiple installments in ascending order.

testDesign.positive: Three installments carry 01,02,03 in submission order.
testDesign.negative: Change only third sequence to 01; observe nonascending installment sequence.
testDesign.boundary: Two-digit width and an equal consecutive value; starting number, increment size and wraparound are not defined.
testDesign.notes: Do not invent mandatory increment-by-one or wrap 99 to 00.

rules.statement: MasterCard-only category/subcategory 09 is four alphanumeric bytes: C101 CIT adhoc credential-on-file, C102 CIT standing order variable amount/fixed frequency, C103 CIT subscription fixed amount/fixed frequency, C104 CIT installment; M101 MIT unscheduled COF, M102 MIT standing order variable amount/fixed frequency, M103 MIT subscription fixed amount/fixed frequency, M104 MIT installment.

testDesign.positive: MasterCard merchant-initiated fixed-amount fixed-frequency subscription uses M103; independently pair all eight scenarios with their source code.
testDesign.negative: Change only M103 to C103 while retaining merchant-initiated preconditions; observe initiator mismatch despite a listed code.
testDesign.boundary: Four bytes; C105/M105 unlisted; Visa with C101 is outside brand scope.
testDesign.notes: Discover/Visa-only fields 01-08 must not be inferred as MasterCard requirements from the generic table title.

rules.statement: Visa India recurring Payment Type 12 is one digit: 1 registration/first transaction, 2 subsequent, 3 modification, 4 cancellation. It is required and should be sent only for India-issued Visa recurring payments.

testDesign.positive: Visa India recurring registration uses 1; fixtures for later debit, change and revocation use 2,3,4 respectively.
testDesign.negative: Change only cancellation event value 4 to 2; observe event mismatch.
testDesign.boundary: 1 and 4 valid endpoints; 0/5 unlisted; omit only 12 to test contextual requiredness.
testDesign.notes: The parameter Payment Type is sub-table 02 F/V; do not confuse it with event sub-table 12.

rules.statement: A Visa India subsequent recurring transaction at or below equivalent INR 15,000 is non-ecommerce, omits CAVV, uses recurring event 2 and Table 013 R. Above equivalent INR 15,000 it is ecommerce with Table 030 terminal type 25, CAVV, event 2 and Table 013 R.

testDesign.positive: Previously registered/authenticated/authorized India Visa account: INR 15000 subsequent uses event 2,R,non-ecommerce and no CAVV; INR 15000.01 uses event 2,R,terminal 25,ecommerce and CAVV.
testDesign.negative: Remove only CAVV from the greater-than-threshold fixture; observe missing required cryptogram.
testDesign.boundary: 14999.99/15000.00/15000.01 INR with the currency amount quantum explicit; converted currency fixtures need an approved conversion source.
testDesign.notes: No exchange-rate source or future RBI threshold is invented. Review Table 030/035/Y representation and Q's nonrecurring wording.

rules.statement: Changing any of total payment count, Payment Type, MIT Amount or Frequency for Visa India recurring requires an ecommerce modification transaction with event 3, Table 030 terminal type 25, CAVV and recurring indicator R.

testDesign.positive: Change only frequency from monthly 04 to weekly 02 and send event 3,ecommerce,terminal 25,CAVV,R; repeat independently for each of the other three parameters.
testDesign.negative: Change only event 3 to 2 while modifying frequency; observe modification identification discrepancy.
testDesign.boundary: Even a below-INR-15000 modification uses authentication; unchanged parameters alone do not establish a modification trigger.
testDesign.notes: Validation flag history permits modification values but it is not explicitly one of these four triggering parameters.

rules.statement: Cancellation of a previously established Visa India recurring payment is an ecommerce zero-dollar account-verification transaction with event 4, Table 030 terminal type 25, CAVV and recurring indicator R.

testDesign.positive: Established India Visa agreement cancellation uses account verification amount zero,event 4,ecommerce,terminal 25,CAVV,R.
testDesign.negative: Change only amount from zero to one currency minor unit; observe zero-amount cancellation discrepancy.
testDesign.boundary: Zero is exact, not below-threshold debit; omit CAVV separately to test authentication regardless of zero amount.
testDesign.notes: No cancellation success response or issuer behavior is specified in this layout.

rules.statement: Visa India recurring first registration/transaction needs additional-factor authentication. Later recurring payments require a successfully registered card and a first transaction that was successfully authenticated and authorized. Modification or revocation also needs additional-factor authentication; above-threshold subsequent payments require it and ecommerce identification.

testDesign.positive: History contains successful registration, first authentication and first authorization before subsequent INR 100 debit without additional-factor authentication.
testDesign.negative: Change only first-authorization history to failed; observe missing prerequisite for subsequent debit.
testDesign.boundary: First registration and modification/revocation require authentication even below the subsequent-debit limit; change one prerequisite at a time.
testDesign.notes: Global BIN File subscription is encouraged, not mandatory. INR 15000 is release-specific and source warns of future RBI revision.

rules.statement: Visa India recurring requests must include Table 056 data and Table 013 recurring indicator. Registration Reference Number 13 is a unique recurring-payment reference of exactly 35 alphanumeric bytes, required only for this scope; if initially supplied it stays present and unchanged on all subsequent requests.

testDesign.positive: Initial reference is 35 repeated A characters; subsequent and modification fixtures carry exactly the same reference and R.
testDesign.negative: Change only one reference character on a subsequent request; observe initial-reference history discrepancy.
testDesign.boundary: 35 versus 34/36 bytes; removing only R tests companion presence independently.
testDesign.notes: Table 013 R additionally requires credit type 020 and eligible BIN as documented in its own layout.

rules.statement: When an authenticated Visa recurring scenario carries CAVV using Table 035, that referenced layout orders twenty raw binary XID bytes before twenty raw binary CAVV bytes, with maximum forty bytes. Do not send textual hexadecimal or base64 in place of the raw layout. Appendix Y separately distinguishes revised CAVV Element 195 and token TAVV Element 237; it does not make these fields interchangeable.

applicability.condition: CAVV required and Table 035 representation chosen

testDesign.positive: Forty-byte structural fixture is twenty raw 0x01 XID bytes followed by twenty raw 0x02 CAVV bytes, with Table 035 declared count 040; authenticate it only with an authorized network fixture in later execution.
testDesign.negative: Replace only the raw payload representation with its eighty-character hexadecimal text and adjust its count; observe violation of binary representation and forty-byte maximum.
testDesign.boundary: XID20 plus CAVV20; independently truncate one part by one byte. Include a raw 0x2B byte in a counted structural fixture to ensure printable separator characters are not used to terminate binary content.
testDesign.notes: Table 035 prose says variable up to40 while listing two20-byte components; do not infer arbitrary shorter cryptograms. Segment123 revised CAVV is a separate alternative requiring the Appendix Y scenario and availability check; no cryptographic validity is asserted.

rules.statement: The referenced Table 030 POS Condition Code is required for all Credential-on-File, EMV and internet/mobile/ecommerce/in-app transactions, including a recurring credential-on-file request below the additional-authentication threshold. Its ten-character payload uses terminal type at positions9-10; Visa values25 or26 require CAVV. Omitting CAVV for eligible below-threshold subsequent recurring does not waive Table030's credential-on-file presence rule.

applicability.table056Context: stored-credential requests when corresponding context holds

testDesign.positive: Registered India-issued Visa subsequent COF debit INR100 contains a ten-byte Table030 fixture using a reviewed non-ecommerce terminal code, alongside event2,R and no CAVV; independent EMV request also contains030.
testDesign.negative: Remove only Table030 from the below-threshold COF fixture; observe missing required POS Condition Code despite no additional CAVV requirement.
testDesign.boundary: Compare COF and non-COF/non-EMV/non-internet contexts; Table030 is optional for the latter under its own rule. Mutate Visa terminal type to25 without CAVV separately.
testDesign.notes: Appendix I-19 position list omits position3 while Appendix Q describes terminal class positions1-3. Resolve source layout and code selection before serialized execution; no EMV chip cryptogram layout is invented in this batch.

notes.statement: Sub-table ID allocation 01-24 and generic maximum 35 bytes do not define entries 10,11 or 14-24; no such nested layouts are added.
Discover/Visa scopes, first-payment-only restrictions and Visa India history rules are intentionally retained separately. Not every sub-table is necessary for every MIT/CIT.
Visa India issuer identification can benefit from Global BIN File subscription; RBI may revise the INR limit. No revised threshold or currency conversion method is provided.

rules.statement: For Discover third-party payment providers, Table 057 represents the underlying retailer's merchant city, not the provider's city. Retain An20 and the stated two-byte N2 length attribute without silently converting it to common Element 112's n3.

testDesign.positive: Provider is in Boston and underlying retailer in Denver; logical merchant city is Denver.
